definition: Of, relating to, or characteristic of regions of perpetual snow; growing or living in or under snow.
etymology: From Latin nivalis, snowy, itself from nix, nivis, snow. The same root that gave English niveous and fed into the name of Nivôse, the snowy month of the French Revolutionary calendar. It arrived in English botanical and geographical writing in the nineteenth century, carried in by naturalists describing alpine plant zones where snow never fully retreats.
usage: The nival zone above the treeline was still unmarked by any boot, the snow lying in that particular undisturbed silence that belongs entirely to itself.
